questions.title: Nematode causing different types of anaemia
questions.question: Different types of anaemia may occur in infection with:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Diphyllobothrium latum causes a single, specific anaemia — megaloblastic (vitamin-B12-deficiency) anaemia from competition for B12 — not 'different types'.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Fasciola is a liver fluke; anaemia is not its characteristic haematological feature.
explanations.C: Correct. Strongyloides stercoralis is the nematode in which SEVERAL types of anaemia may occur: chronic infection produces intestinal malabsorption and chronic blood/protein loss, so an affected patient may develop iron-deficiency (microcytic) anaemia, megaloblastic (folate/B12-malabsorption) anaemia and the anaemia of chronic disease. The breadth of malabsorption and the possibility of hyperinfection in the immunosuppressed is why 'different types of anaemia' points specifically to Strongyloides rather than to a worm that causes one defined anaemia. This distinguishes it from hookworm (iron-deficiency only) and Diphyllobothrium (B12 only).
explanations.D: Incorrect. Necator americanus (hookworm) causes one defined picture — iron-deficiency (microcytic hypochromic) anaemia from chronic intestinal blood loss — not different types.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that Strongyloides stercoralis, through malabsorption and chronic loss, can cause several different types of anaemia.

questions.title: Route of Strongyloides infection
questions.question: Individuals contract Strongyloides stercoralis via which of the following?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ingestion of infected freshwater fish transmits Diphyllobothrium latum (plerocercoid), not Strongyloides.
explanations.B: Correct. Strongyloides stercoralis is acquired when infective FILARIFORM larvae in the soil actively penetrate intact skin (typically bare feet), exactly as hookworm larvae do. From the skin the larvae enter the circulation, migrate through the lungs, are swallowed and mature in the small intestine. Skin penetration by soil filariform larvae is therefore the mode of infection, and it also explains larva currens and the risk of autoinfection.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Strongyloides is not vector-borne; no insect bite is involved.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Ingestion of contaminated (undercooked) beef transmits the beef tapeworm Taenia saginata, not Strongyloides.

questions.learning_objective: Identify skin penetration by filariform larvae as the route of Strongyloides stercoralis infection.

questions.title: Not a Trichostrongylus control strategy
questions.question: Which of the following is not a Trichostrongylus colubriformis prevention and control strategy?

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS a valid strategy). Trichostrongylus is acquired by swallowing larvae on contaminated water or plants, so proper water treatment does help prevent it.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it IS a valid strategy). The larvae are ingested on contaminated vegetables, so appropriate food handling and washing of produce reduce transmission.
explanations.C: Correct. Use of insect repellent is NOT a control strategy for Trichostrongylus colubriformis because the worm is not transmitted by any insect vector — infection is acquired by the faecal-oral route, ingesting infective larvae on contaminated water, soil or plants. Control therefore rests on sanitation, safe water and food hygiene, and repelling insects does nothing to interrupt this non-vector, oral cycle. This is the odd-one-out among the listed measures.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS a valid strategy). Because transmission is faecal-oral from soil contaminated with faeces, proper sanitation practices break the cycle.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that Trichostrongylus is transmitted by the faecal-oral route, so insect repellent is not a control strategy.

questions.title: Parasite causing pruritus ani
questions.question: Pruritis ani is found with:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Trichuriasis (whipworm) causes colitis and, when heavy, rectal prolapse — not the perianal itch of pinworm.
explanations.B: Correct. Pruritus ani (perianal itching, worst at night) is the hallmark of Enterobiasis. The gravid female Enterobius vermicularis migrates out of the anus at night to deposit her sticky eggs on the perianal skin, and the local irritation plus a hypersensitivity reaction to the eggs produces intense nocturnal itching. Scratching then transfers eggs to the fingers and perpetuates auto-reinfection. This nocturnal perianal itch is the classic clinical clue to pinworm.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Toxocariasis causes visceral/ocular larva migrans with eosinophilia, not perianal itch.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Ancylostomiasis (hookworm) causes ground itch at the site of skin penetration and iron-deficiency anaemia, not pruritus ani.

questions.learning_objective: Associate nocturnal pruritus ani with Enterobius vermicularis (enterobiasis).

questions.title: Parasite causing rectal prolapse
questions.question: Rectal prolapse is a feature in infection with:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ascaris causes intestinal obstruction and biliary/pulmonary manifestations, not rectal prolapse.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Enterobius causes perianal pruritus, not prolapse.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Strongyloides causes larva currens, malabsorption and hyperinfection, not rectal prolapse.
explanations.D: Correct. Rectal prolapse is the classic feature of heavy Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) infection, characteristically in malnourished children. The adult worms thread their thin anterior ends into the mucosa of the rectum and colon, and a heavy worm burden with chronic straining (tenesmus) and inflammation causes the rectal mucosa to prolapse, sometimes with worms visible on its surface. This makes rectal prolapse a diagnostic clue to massive trichuriasis.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise rectal prolapse as a feature of heavy Trichuris trichiura infection.

questions.title: Diagnostic stage of Strongyloides in stool
questions.question: The typical diagnostic stage of Strongyloides stercoralis seen in stool is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Unlike hookworm, Strongyloides eggs hatch within the intestinal mucosa, so mature eggs are not usually found in stool.
explanations.B: Correct. The typical diagnostic stage of Strongyloides stercoralis in fresh stool is the RHABDITIFORM (first-stage) larva. Because the eggs hatch in the intestinal wall, it is the rhabditiform larva — not the egg — that is passed and recovered on stool examination (or by the Baermann/agar-plate techniques). It is distinguished from a hookworm rhabditiform larva by its short buccal cavity and prominent genital primordium, which is the key morphological point tested.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The filariform larva is the infective soil/tissue stage (and appears in autoinfection); it is not the usual stool diagnostic stage.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Immature eggs are not the stool finding for Strongyloides because the eggs hatch in the mucosa before being passed.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the rhabditiform larva as the diagnostic stage of Strongyloides stercoralis in stool.

questions.title: Helminth with internal autoinfection
questions.question: Internal autoinfection occurs with the following:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ascaris eggs must embryonate in soil for weeks before becoming infective, so no autoinfection occurs.
explanations.B: Correct. Capillaria philippinensis is characterised by INTERNAL autoinfection: some females are larviparous and produce larvae that develop and reinfect the same host's intestine without leaving the body. This internal multiplication causes progressive build-up of worms, producing the severe, protein-losing enteropathy and hyperinfection that can be fatal if untreated. Among the listed nematodes, this autoinfective capacity is unique to Capillaria philippinensis (a feature it shares in principle only with Strongyloides).
explanations.C: Incorrect. Trichuris eggs need to embryonate in soil; there is no autoinfection.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Trichostrongylus is acquired by ingesting soil/plant larvae and does not autoinfect.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise internal autoinfection (larvipary) as a feature of Capillaria philippinensis.

questions.hold: printed key A (Ascaris lumbricoides) but the stem specifies 'the following ADULT helminth may cause pulmonary manifestations' — Ascaris pulmonary manifestations (Loeffler syndrome) are produced by the migrating LARVAE during the lung phase, not by the adult worm; stem/parasitology mismatch, held for human adjudication (never author to a wrong fact).

questions.title: Most common feature of visceral larva migrans
questions.question: The most common characteristic of visceral larva migrans is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Lymphadenitis is not the defining feature of visceral larva migrans.
explanations.B: Correct. The most common and characteristic feature of visceral larva migrans (usually caused by Toxocara canis/cati larvae) is a persistent, marked CHRONIC EOSINOPHILIA. Non-human larvae wander through the viscera (liver, lungs, occasionally brain and eye) and cannot mature, and the host mounts a sustained type-2/eosinophilic response to the migrating larvae, giving high blood eosinophil counts often with hepatomegaly and hypergammaglobulinaemia. This chronic eosinophilia is the laboratory hallmark that flags the diagnosis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Seizures may occur if larvae reach the CNS but are uncommon, not the most common feature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A non-specific leucocytosis is far less characteristic than the eosinophilia that defines the syndrome.

questions.module_subject: 309 INF > Parasitology > Nematoda > Toxocara (visceral larva migrans)
questions.learning_objective: Identify chronic eosinophilia as the most common feature of visceral larva migrans.

questions.title: Pair of parasites related to the pig
questions.question: Pig is related to infection with which pair of parasites?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Taenia saginata is the beef tapeworm (cattle, not pig), and Trichostrongylus is a soil/plant-borne nematode unrelated to pigs.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Although Taenia solium is the pork tapeworm, Ascaris lumbricoides is a human soil-transmitted roundworm not related to the pig.
explanations.C: Correct. The pig is the source/reservoir for BOTH members of this pair. Balantidium coli, the only ciliate pathogen of man, has the pig as its main reservoir host (humans are infected by cysts from pig faeces), and Taenia solium is the PORK tapeworm, acquired by eating undercooked pork containing Cysticercus cellulosae. Both organisms are therefore epidemiologically tied to pigs, which is what makes this the correct pair.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Balantidium coli is pig-related, but Entamoeba coli is a harmless human commensal amoeba with no pig association, so the pair is wrong.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise the pig as the reservoir/source for both Balantidium coli and Taenia solium.

questions.hold: printed key B (Toxocara cati) but the stem 'Peri-orbital oedema, fever, eosinophilia' is the classic diagnostic triad of Trichinella spiralis, which is not among the four options; the printed key is the best-of-offered eosinophilic-tissue nematode but the periorbital-oedema triad is misassigned, held for human adjudication.

questions.title: Internal and external autoinfection
questions.question: Internal and external autoinfection occurs with:

explanations.A: Correct. Strongyloides stercoralis is the nematode showing BOTH internal and external autoinfection. In internal autoinfection, rhabditiform larvae mature to infective filariform larvae inside the gut and re-penetrate the intestinal mucosa; in external autoinfection they re-penetrate the perianal skin. Both routes let the parasite complete new cycles without leaving the host, which allows lifelong persistence and, in the immunosuppressed, life-threatening hyperinfection. This dual (internal AND external) autoinfection distinguishes Strongyloides from Capillaria, which shows internal autoinfection only.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Capillaria philippinensis shows INTERNAL autoinfection (larvipary) only, not external.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Trichuris does not autoinfect; its eggs must embryonate in soil.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Trichostrongylus is acquired from soil/plants and does not autoinfect.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that Strongyloides stercoralis shows both internal and external autoinfection.

questions.title: Nematode diagnosed by MRCP
questions.question: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography may be used in diagnosing some cases of infection with:

explanations.A: Correct. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) is useful in biliary ASCARIASIS, a complication of Ascaris lumbricoides. Adult Ascaris worms can migrate up from the duodenum through the ampulla into the biliary tree or pancreatic duct, causing biliary colic, cholangitis or pancreatitis, and MRCP demonstrates the worm as a linear filling defect within the ducts. This ability of the large adult worm to invade the biliary tree is why an imaging study of the bile ducts helps diagnose it, unlike the other, purely intestinal nematodes listed.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Capillaria philippinensis is a small-bowel worm causing protein-losing enteropathy; it does not enter the biliary tree, so MRCP is not used.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Trichuris lives in the caecum/colon and is not a biliary parasite.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Ancylostoma duodenale lives attached to small-intestinal mucosa and is diagnosed by stool eggs, not MRCP.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise MRCP as an imaging aid in biliary ascariasis (Ascaris lumbricoides).

questions.title: Diagnostic tool for trichuriasis
questions.question: The following is a diagnostic tool for trichuriasis:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The NIH (cellophane) swab is used to recover Enterobius vermicularis eggs from the perianal skin, not for Trichuris.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The string test (Enterotest) recovers duodenal parasites such as Giardia and Strongyloides, not the caecal whipworm.
explanations.C: Correct. Proctoscopy (or sigmoidoscopy) is a diagnostic tool for trichuriasis. In heavy Trichuris trichiura infection the thin adult whipworms are visible on endoscopy studding the inflamed rectal and colonic mucosa, and they are seen directly on the surface of a prolapsed rectum. Direct visualisation of the worms on proctoscopy therefore confirms the diagnosis alongside finding the barrel-shaped bipolar-plugged eggs in stool.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Bronchial lavage recovers larvae of lung-migrating parasites (e.g. Ascaris, Strongyloides in hyperinfection), not the intestinal whipworm.

questions.learning_objective: Identify proctoscopy as a diagnostic tool for trichuriasis.

questions.title: Nematode not exclusively oral in transmission
questions.question: The following parasite is NOT exclusively transmitted by the oral route:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ascaris is acquired only by swallowing embryonated eggs — an exclusively oral route.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Fasciola gigantica is acquired only by ingesting metacercariae on aquatic plants — an exclusively oral route.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hymenolepis nana is acquired by ingesting eggs (directly infective); its transmission is oral.
explanations.D: Correct. Enterobius vermicularis is NOT exclusively transmitted by the oral route. Besides the usual faecal-oral ingestion of eggs, it also spreads by RETROINFECTION (larvae hatching on the perianal skin migrate back up through the anus into the intestine) and by inhalation of airborne eggs from contaminated bedding/dust. Because these additional non-oral routes exist, pinworm is the exception among the listed parasites whose spread is not limited to swallowing.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that Enterobius vermicularis spreads by retroinfection and inhalation, not exclusively by the oral route.

questions.title: Protein-energy malnutrition feature
questions.question: Protein energy malnutrition is a feature in:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Trichuriasis is associated with colitis, dysentery and rectal prolapse; growth retardation can occur but PEM is not its listed hallmark here.
explanations.B: Correct. Protein-energy malnutrition is a recognised feature of ASCARIASIS. A heavy Ascaris lumbricoides burden in children competes for ingested food, impairs digestion and absorption of protein, fat and vitamins, and reduces appetite, so chronic heavy infection contributes to protein-energy malnutrition and growth retardation. This nutritional impact is greatest where large worm loads occur in already under-nourished children, which is why ascariasis is the answer.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Fascioliasis is a hepatobiliary fluke disease (liver damage, biliary obstruction), not a PEM syndrome.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Halzoun is an acute pharyngeal irritation from Linguatula/Fasciola in the throat, unrelated to protein-energy malnutrition.

questions.learning_objective: Associate protein-energy malnutrition with heavy Ascaris lumbricoides infection.

questions.title: Nematode causing iron-deficiency anaemia
questions.question: Iron deficiency anaemia may be seen with:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cyclospora cayetanensis causes watery diarrhoea in the immunocompromised, not iron-deficiency anaemia.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Enterobius causes perianal pruritus and does not suck blood, so it does not cause iron-deficiency anaemia.
explanations.C: Correct. Iron-deficiency (microcytic hypochromic) anaemia is the classic feature of hookworm, Ancylostoma duodenale. The adult worms attach to the small-intestinal mucosa and actively suck blood, and each worm removes a small but steady amount of blood daily, so a heavy chronic burden causes continuous intestinal blood loss and depletes body iron stores. The resulting iron-deficiency anaemia is the hallmark of ancylostomiasis and correlates with worm load.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Strongyloides causes malabsorption and can give several anaemias, but chronic blood-sucking iron loss is the defining mechanism of hookworm, not Strongyloides.

questions.learning_objective: Associate iron-deficiency anaemia with the blood-sucking hookworm Ancylostoma duodenale.

questions.title: Transmission of Capillaria philippinensis
questions.question: Capillariasis philippinensis is transmitted by:

options.D: Accidental swallowing of an infected flea

explanations.A: Correct. Capillaria philippinensis is transmitted by EATING raw or improperly cooked infected freshwater fish (the small fish that harbour the infective larvae). Once eaten, the larvae develop in the human small intestine, and because females are larviparous the worm multiplies by internal autoinfection, causing severe malabsorption and protein-losing enteropathy. Undercooked freshwater fish is therefore the source of infection.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Accidental swallowing of an infected Cyclops transmits Diphyllobothrium/Dracunculus, not Capillaria philippinensis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Improperly cooked pork transmits Taenia solium/Trichinella, not Capillaria.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Swallowing an infected flea transmits Hymenolepis/Dipylidium cestodes, not Capillaria.

questions.learning_objective: Identify eating infected freshwater fish as the route of Capillaria philippinensis infection.

questions.title: Parasite of larva currens
questions.question: "Larva currens" is the name given to the migrating larva of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ancylostoma larvae in skin cause a localised, slow-moving ground itch, not the rapid larva currens.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Trichostrongylus does not produce a creeping cutaneous larval track.
explanations.C: Correct. 'Larva currens' (running larva) is the name for the rapidly migrating cutaneous larval track of Strongyloides stercoralis. In external autoinfection, filariform larvae re-penetrate the perianal skin and race through it at up to several centimetres per hour, producing a fast-moving, itchy, urticarial serpiginous streak — much faster than the cutaneous larva migrans of animal hookworms. This speed is why it is called larva currens and it is characteristic of Strongyloides autoinfection.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Capillaria philippinensis remains in the gut and produces no migrating skin larva.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise larva currens as the rapidly migrating cutaneous larva of Strongyloides stercoralis.

questions.title: Infective stage of Ancylostoma duodenale
questions.question: Concerning ancylostomiasis duodenale, which of the following is infective:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The egg is the diagnostic stool stage, not the infective stage; it hatches in soil to release larvae.
explanations.B: Correct. The infective stage of Ancylostoma duodenale (hookworm) is the FILARIFORM (third-stage) larva. Eggs passed in stool hatch in warm moist soil into rhabditiform larvae, which feed and moult twice into non-feeding filariform larvae; these infective filariform larvae penetrate intact skin (or, for A. duodenale, may also be swallowed) to start a new infection. The filariform larva is therefore the stage that infects man.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The rhabditiform larva is the feeding soil stage that precedes the infective form; it is not itself infective.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The adult worm lives in the human small intestine and is not a stage that transmits infection.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the filariform larva as the infective stage of Ancylostoma duodenale.

questions.title: Chronic diarrhoea after eating undercooked fish
questions.question: A patient presenting with chronic diarrhoea and a history of eating improperly cooked whole infected fish may be infected with:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Enterobius vermicularis is acquired by faecal-oral ingestion of eggs and causes perianal pruritus, not a fish-borne chronic diarrhoea.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Echinococcus granulosus is acquired from dog faeces and forms hydatid cysts in the liver/lung; it is not fish-borne and does not cause chronic diarrhoea.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Ascaris lumbricoides is acquired by swallowing embryonated eggs from soil, not from fish, and causes obstruction and malnutrition rather than fish-linked chronic diarrhoea.
explanations.D: Correct. Capillaria philippinensis is acquired by eating raw or improperly cooked infected freshwater fish that harbour the larvae. In the small intestine the females are larviparous and multiply by internal autoinfection, so the worm burden climbs and produces a severe, chronic, protein-losing enteropathy with watery diarrhoea, malabsorption and wasting. The history of eating undercooked whole fish followed by chronic diarrhoea therefore points to intestinal capillariasis.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise intestinal capillariasis (Capillaria philippinensis) in a patient with chronic diarrhoea after eating undercooked freshwater fish.

questions.title: Risk of walking barefoot
questions.question: Walking barefooted poses a risk of acquiring:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Trichostrongylus is acquired by swallowing larvae on contaminated water or plants (faecal-oral), not by skin penetration of bare feet.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Visceral larva migrans follows ingestion of Toxocara eggs (from soil contaminated by dog/cat faeces), not skin penetration while barefoot.
explanations.C: Correct. Walking barefoot exposes the skin to soil containing infective filariform larvae of the hookworm Ancylostoma duodenale (and Necator), which actively penetrate intact skin, typically of the feet. From the skin they enter the circulation, migrate through the lungs and mature in the small intestine. Because transmission depends on skin contact with contaminated soil, wearing footwear is a simple preventive measure and going barefoot is the classic risk for ancylostomiasis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Intestinal capillariasis is acquired by eating infected freshwater fish, not by skin penetration when barefoot.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise walking barefoot as the risk for hookworm (ancylostomiasis) acquired by filariform-larva skin penetration.

questions.title: Disseminated infection in AIDS
questions.question: Disseminated systemic infection in an AIDS patient is reported with:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Trichostrongylus cannot autoinfect and remains a mild intestinal infection; it does not disseminate in immunosuppression.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Enterobius causes perianal pruritus and does not multiply within or disseminate through the host.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hookworm larvae complete their migration and mature in the gut without autoinfection, so ancylostomiasis does not cause disseminated systemic disease.
explanations.D: Correct. Strongyloides stercoralis is the nematode that causes disseminated (hyperinfection) systemic disease in the immunosuppressed AIDS patient. Because it can complete internal autoinfection, it persists for years, and when cell-mediated immunity fails the autoinfective cycle accelerates uncontrollably so that filariform larvae spread from the gut throughout the body, carrying enteric bacteria to the lungs, brain and other organs. This disseminated strongyloidiasis is frequently fatal, which is why the worm must be sought and treated before immunosuppression.

questions.learning_objective: Associate disseminated (hyperinfection) strongyloidiasis with the immunosuppressed or AIDS patient.

questions.title: Nematode infecting by skin penetration
questions.question: Which of the following parasites infects man by skin penetration?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Trichostrongylus colubriformis is acquired by swallowing infective larvae on contaminated plants or water, not by skin penetration.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Enterobius vermicularis is acquired by ingesting eggs (and by retroinfection), not by larvae penetrating the skin.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Trichuris trichiura is acquired by swallowing embryonated eggs from soil; there is no skin-penetration stage.
explanations.D: Correct. Strongyloides stercoralis infects man when infective filariform larvae in the soil actively penetrate intact skin, exactly as hookworm larvae do. After penetrating the skin the larvae enter the circulation, migrate through the lungs, are swallowed and mature in the small intestine. This percutaneous route also underlies external autoinfection and the rapidly migrating skin track called larva currens, so skin penetration is the mode of infection for Strongyloides among the worms listed.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Strongyloides stercoralis as the listed nematode that infects man by skin penetration.

questions.title: Cause of maldigestion in ascariasis
questions.question: Maldigestion is seen with ascariasis due to:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Multivitamin deficiency is a consequence of poor nutrition in heavy infection, not the mechanism that causes the maldigestion.
explanations.B: Incorrect. There is no anti-IgA blocking antibody mechanism in ascariasis; this is not how the worm impairs digestion.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Chronic mucosal malabsorption is the mechanism seen with Strongyloides and Capillaria, whereas Ascaris impairs luminal digestion, so this describes malabsorption rather than the maldigestion asked about.
explanations.D: Correct. Maldigestion in ascariasis is due to the adult worm's secretion of anti-enzyme substances such as antitrypsin and other protease inhibitors, which neutralise the host's digestive enzymes in the gut lumen. With digestion of protein and other nutrients inhibited, food is poorly broken down, giving maldigestion that is distinct from the mucosal malabsorption of other worms. In a heavy worm burden this luminal enzyme inhibition contributes to the nutritional impairment of ascariasis.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute the maldigestion of ascariasis to the worm's secretion of anti-enzymes.

questions.title: Cause of fatal complications of ascariasis
questions.question: Serious and sometimes fatal complications of ascariasis are due to:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Toxic or enzymatic activity contributes to maldigestion but is not the cause of the life-threatening complications.
explanations.B: Correct. The serious and sometimes fatal complications of ascariasis are due to migration of the ADULT worms. A tangled bolus of worms can cause intestinal obstruction or volvulus, and single worms migrating through the ampulla cause biliary obstruction, cholangitis, pancreatitis or hepatic abscess, while entry into the appendix causes appendicitis. These mechanical adult-worm events, rather than the eggs or larvae, produce the dangerous disease.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Ascaris eggs are passed in the stool and are not trapped in tissues (unlike schistosome eggs), so they do not cause these complications.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Larval migration through the lungs causes only the transient Loeffler (pulmonary) phase, not the serious mechanical complications.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that the serious and fatal complications of ascariasis result from migration of the adult worms.

questions.title: Infection controlled by mass treatment
questions.question: Mass treatment is one of the control measures against infection with:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Amoebiasis is a protozoal infection controlled mainly by safe water and sanitation, not by community mass deworming.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cryptosporidiosis is a protozoal, often self-limiting infection with no effective mass-treatment programme.
explanations.C: Correct. Mass (population) treatment, that is periodic community-wide deworming with albendazole or mebendazole, is a recognised control measure against ascariasis and the other soil-transmitted helminths. Treating the whole at-risk community lowers the average worm burden and egg output, so soil contamination and onward transmission fall. It works because Ascaris has a simple direct soil cycle that responds to reducing the human reservoir.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Fascioliasis is a food-borne fluke controlled by avoiding contaminated aquatic plants and by snail control, not by mass deworming of the population.

questions.learning_objective: Identify mass treatment (community deworming) as a control measure against ascariasis.

questions.title: Seizures, cough and retinal mass
questions.question: Seizures, cough and a unilateral retinal mass could be presenting symptoms of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Trichuriasis causes colitis, dysentery and rectal prolapse, not neurological, pulmonary and ocular disease.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Amoebiasis causes dysentery and, when it spreads, a liver abscess, not a retinal mass with seizures.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Balantidiasis is a colonic infection causing dysentery, not multi-organ larval migration.
explanations.D: Correct. Seizures, cough and a unilateral retinal mass together point to visceral (and ocular) larva migrans caused by the larvae of the dog/cat ascarid Toxocara. The larvae cannot mature in man and wander through organs: in the brain they can cause seizures, in the lungs cough and wheeze, and in the eye an inflammatory retinal granuloma that appears as a unilateral retinal mass, sometimes mistaken for retinoblastoma. This multi-organ larval migration explains the combination of symptoms.

questions.module_subject: 309 INF > Parasitology > Nematoda > Toxocara (visceral larva migrans)
questions.learning_objective: Recognise seizures, cough and a unilateral retinal mass as presentations of Toxocara visceral and ocular larva migrans.

questions.title: Melena and occult blood in stool
questions.question: Melena and occult blood in the stool could be a manifestation of:

explanations.A: Correct. Melena and occult blood in the stool are manifestations of ancylostomiasis (hookworm). The adult Ancylostoma duodenale worms attach to the small-intestinal mucosa and actively suck blood, and they also move to fresh sites leaving bleeding points, so there is continuous intestinal blood loss that appears as occult blood or, when heavy, as melena. This chronic blood loss is also what produces the iron-deficiency anaemia of hookworm disease.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Enterobius does not suck blood; it causes perianal pruritus, not gastrointestinal bleeding.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Taeniasis (adult tapeworm) usually causes mild abdominal symptoms and proglottids in stool, not melena or occult blood.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cystoisospora (Cystoisosporiasis) causes watery diarrhoea, especially in the immunocompromised, not bloody stool.

questions.learning_objective: Associate melena and occult blood in stool with the blood-sucking hookworm (ancylostomiasis).

questions.title: Prevention by proper cooking of pork
questions.question: Proper cooking of pig meat is a preventive measure against:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fascioliasis is acquired from metacercariae on aquatic plants, so cooking pork does not prevent it.
explanations.B: Correct. Proper cooking of pig meat prevents Trichinella spiralis infection, because the worm is acquired by eating raw or undercooked pork containing encysted infective larvae and thorough cooking kills those larvae. Man is a dead-end host who develops an early enteral phase of diarrhoea followed by a parenteral phase of myositis, periorbital oedema and eosinophilia as new larvae encyst in muscle. Adequate cooking of the meat therefore interrupts transmission.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Taeniasis saginata is the BEEF tapeworm, acquired from undercooked beef, so cooking pork does not prevent it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Coenurosis is acquired by ingesting eggs of Taenia multiceps from dog faeces, not from eating pork.

questions.learning_objective: Identify proper cooking of pork as the preventive measure against Trichinella spiralis.
